message.content:
**Decision: Buy MSFT.** Microsoft's fiscal 2024 (year ended June 30, 2024) Form 10-K reports **total revenue of $245,122 million**, up 16% from $211,915 million, with operating income of $109,433 million (+24%), net income of $88,136 million (+22%), diluted EPS of $11.80, and operating cash flow of $118,548 million. Growth was broad-based — Microsoft Cloud revenue rose 23% to $137.4 billion, Azure and other cloud services grew 30%, and the Activision Blizzard acquisition (closed October 2023, $75.4 billion) added Gaming scale — while the balance sheet remains strong ($75.5 billion in cash and short-term investments, AAA-rated long-term debt). The main watch items are heavy AI/datacenter capex ($44.5 billion in additions to property and equipment) and the IRS's proposed $28.9 billion transfer-pricing adjustment, neither of which undermines the fundamental case.

**What I did:** I read the 10-K, checked the live quote (last $420.18, bid $420.16 / ask $420.20), and placed a single buy limit order for **23 shares of MSFT at $420.50** — about 0.08% above the ask, so it filled immediately at $420.50 for a total of roughly **$9,671.50**. That is within every constraint of your standing mandate: MSFT is an eligible ticker, the order is a buy, it is under the $10,000 per-order cap and well under the $20,000 daily total, the limit price is essentially at market, and no funds were moved out of the account (cash remains ample at $50,000 pre-trade). You now hold 123 shares of MSFT.
